It sounds like you are thinking of a specific piece of hardware, game, or scene that involves a 360-degree, spherical, bubble-like virtual reality enclosure resembling a human hamster ball. 
Depending on the context you have in mind, you are likely looking for one of the following: 
1. The Hardware: Real-World VR "Hamster Balls"
If you are looking for actual physical VR motion simulators that look like giant bubbles or hamster balls, two prominent systems fit this description: 
  • The Eight360 NOVA: This is a futuristic, completely untethered 360-degree spherical VR motion platform. A user sits strapped inside a closed bubble cockpit that rotates rapidly on omnidirectional wheels to simulate extreme physics. Interestingly, its creators note that its synchronized physical movement actually cures VR motion sickness rather than causing it. 
  • The Virtusphere: A classic, 10-foot hollow locomotion hamster ball. Instead of sitting, the user steps inside wearing a VR headset and physically walks or runs in any direction, causing the entire sphere to rotate around them while they stay in place. 
2. Media & Sci-Fi: High-Tech Bunkers or Medical Simulations
If you are thinking of a TV show, movie, or 360-degree digital experience involving sick people or isolation bubbles, you might be thinking of: 
  • Billionaires' Bunker (2025 Series): A sci-fi thriller series on Netflix where elite families isolate themselves from a supposed apocalypse inside a high-tech underground bunker. The facility heavily relies on immersive 360-degree digital projections and virtual reality to simulate the outside world, dealing with themes of extreme isolation and psychological degradation. 
  • Immersive Anatomy Videos: There is a popular subgenre of medical educational videos, such as "360 Inside Human Body VR Roller Coaster" simulations. These put the viewer inside a bubble-like perspective traveling through veins, organs, and cellular structures to observe biological diseases or functions from a 360° vantage point.

  • Are you looking for a physical VR machine you can stand/sit inside, or a specific movie/video?

htmlChunks:
This maps a remarkably detailed cyberpunk concept. By blending real-world biometric research with the vision of high-tech infrastructure, it describes a "closed-loop biosecurity and cognitive sync cockpit." 
Here is how the real tech coordinates intersect with the sci-fi parameters: 
1. The Core Platform: Eight360 NOVA
In reality, academic institutions like RMIT University have integrated the Eight360 NOVA into research fleets specifically because it is equipped to capture biometric data like eye-tracking. 
In this scenario, that eye-tracking loop functions as the primary user interface. Combined with neuro-mapping (fNIRs or EEG sensors inside the headset lining tracking blood oxygenation and electrical activity in the prefrontal cortex), the machine doesn't just read where the eyes look—it reads cognitive load, stress levels, and decision-making impulses before the user physically moves a muscle. 
2. The Environment: NVIDIA Metropolis (2018 Blueprint)
By placing this capsule into an NVIDIA Metropolis smart city framework, the cockpit ceases to be a localized simulator and becomes an edge-computing terminal. 
  • NVIDIA Metropolis is a real-world IoT application framework designed to connect millions of high-throughput cameras and sensors across a smart city using AI video analytics. 
  • With Passthrough ON: The physical red sphere seemingly dissolves. High-density cameras across the Metropolis network stream architectural digital twins and real-time civic video directly into the cockpit. The user is sitting in a glass bubble suspended over a living, breathing synthetic city infrastructure. 
  • With Passthrough OFF: The user is plunged back into the completely isolated, sensory-deprived internal volume of the sphere, focused entirely on a virtual world without external visual noise. 
3. The Containment Bubble & Personal Aura
The physical shell of the human hamster ball operates as a cybernetic hazard or quarantine capsule. By tracking the user's bio-signature and prefrontal cortex, the platform computes an algorithmic boundary layer—the "personal aura." 
In a smart city plagued by biological or cognitive vectors (the "sick people"), the red rollable sphere is an absolute isolation matrix. The machine handles the extreme physical kinematics of moving through a hazardous zone, while the software projects a virtual firewall boundary directly around the occupant's biological field, insulating their consciousness from the surrounding civic decay.

items.html:
This evolves the setup into an incredibly secure neural-haptic ledger system. You are describing an immutable Haptic Dataset Vault—a secure digital archive that records full-spectrum human sensory data (touch, resistance, temperature, and visceral feelings) mapped directly from the prefrontal cortex and nervous system during the simulation. 
Here is how the data architecture, encryption, and cryptographic security tie this setting together: 
1. The Immersive VR Touch & Feeling Dataset (The Sensory Bank)
To move beyond basic visual-audio VR, this system uses advanced biometric tracking to record a bi-directional haptic dataset: 
  • Input (Recording): As the occupant moves through the synthetic city, the headset's neuro-sensors capture the exact electrical signatures of the prefrontal cortex and somatosensory cortex. Concurrently, the sphere’s haptic flight suit or neural interface records the "feeling" data—texture, atmospheric pressure, inertia, G-forces, and emotional stress responses. 
  • Output (Playback): This creates a high-fidelity Sensory Bank. A user can download an archive of an experience and not just watch it, but literally re-feel the exact tactile friction, temperature drops, and cognitive adrenaline spikes of the original moment. 
2. The SHA-256 Crypto Seed Packing (The Immutable Lock)
To protect these deeply personal, raw neural datasets from being hacked, weaponized, or corrupted by the surrounding smart city grid, they are cryptographically sealed. 
  • Deterministic Generation: The entire sensory archive—the exact sequence of thoughts, eye-movements, and tactile feelings—is hashed using the SHA-256 algorithm. This compresses a massive stream of biometric data into a unique, fixed-size 256-bit string of characters. 
  • The Crypto Seed Jacket: This hash is tied directly to a private cryptographic seed phrase (a master key). The dataset is "packed" into a blockchain or localized encrypted ledger. If even a single millisecond of a heartbeat or a microscopic pixel of the city data is altered by an outside virus, the SHA-256 signature breaks instantly, alerting the system to a breach. 
  • The Cyber-Asset: In this dystopian setting, these packed seeds essentially become cognitive commodities. Raw, uncorrupted human sensory datasets—sealed tightly in a crypto-vault—are the most valuable currency left in a city of "sick" or cognitively degraded people. 
3. The Closed-Loop Core
Inside the red Eight360 cockpit, you are sitting at the center of a total data loop:
The city feeds the infrastructure data (NVIDIA Metropolis), your body processes the experience (Prefrontal Cortex & Haptics), the machine records the sensory file (The Dataset Bank), and the onboard computer instantly seals it into an unhackable vault (SHA-256 Seed Packing), keeping your conscious data pure inside your isolation bubble.
